items.title: Genetics & Genetic Engineering — the toolkit
items.body:
## Core ideas

- **Genetics** studies heredity and variation; **DNA** carries genes that code for proteins.
- **Genetic engineering** = deliberately altering an organism's DNA. Its foundation is **recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology** — joining DNA from different sources.

## Molecular tools

| Tool | Role |
|---|---|
| Restriction enzymes | 'Molecular scissors' cutting DNA at specific sequences |
| DNA ligase | 'Molecular glue' joining DNA fragments |
| Vectors (plasmids, phages) | Carry the target gene into a host cell |
| PCR | Amplifies a DNA segment into millions of copies |

## Gene editing

- **CRISPR-Cas9** makes precise, targeted DNA cuts; adapted from a bacterial immune system.
- Emmanuelle **Charpentier** and Jennifer **Doudna** won the **2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry**.
- Editing categories: **SDN-1** (no foreign DNA, small indels), **SDN-2** (small template edit), **SDN-3** (large foreign insert = transgenic).
keyPoints: Recombinant DNA technology joins DNA from different sources; it is the basis of genetic engineering.
Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites; DNA ligase joins fragments; plasmids/phages act as vectors.
PCR amplifies a DNA segment into millions of copies (used in RT-PCR COVID tests, forensics).
CRISPR-Cas9 is a precise gene-editing tool; Charpentier and Doudna won the 2020 Chemistry Nobel.
SDN-1 and SDN-2 edits carry no foreign DNA; SDN-3 introduces a foreign gene and is treated as GM.

items.title: GM crops, GEAC & genome-edited rice (2025)
items.body:
## Regulation

- **GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee)** under the **MoEFCC** is the apex body appraising environmental release of GMOs (under Rules 1989 of the Environment Protection Act, 1986).
- **RCGM** (under DBT) oversees research/early trial stages.

## Status of GM crops in India

| Crop | Status |
|---|---|
| **Bt cotton** | Only GM crop under **commercial cultivation** (approved 2002) |
| **Bt brinjal** | Approved 2009, but under **moratorium since 2010** |
| **GM mustard (DMH-11)** | GEAC recommended environmental release (2022); **Supreme Court split verdict, 2024** |

## Genome-edited rice (May 2025)

- India released its **first two genome-edited rice varieties**: **DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala)** — ICAR-IIRR, Hyderabad; **Pusa DST Rice 1** — ICAR-IARI, New Delhi.
- Developed with **SDN-1/SDN-2** editing (no foreign DNA) — **exempt** from GM biosafety rules; aim higher yield, drought tolerance, water/fertiliser saving.
keyPoints: GEAC (under MoEFCC) is the apex regulator for environmental release of GMOs in India.
Bt cotton is India's only commercially cultivated GM crop (approved 2002).
Bt brinjal was approved in 2009 but placed under a moratorium in 2010.
GM mustard DMH-11 got GEAC environmental-release nod in 2022; the Supreme Court gave a split verdict in 2024.
India released its first genome-edited rice varieties — DRR Dhan 100 (Kamala) and Pusa DST Rice 1 — in May 2025 using SDN-1/SDN-2.
items.source: MoEFCC / GEAC; PIB & ICAR — genome-edited rice, May 2025

items.title: Biotech policy & institutions — BioE3, DBT, BIRAC, BRIC
items.body:
## Institutions

- **DBT (Department of Biotechnology)** — nodal department for biotech under the Ministry of Science and Technology.
- **BIRAC** — DBT's public-sector enterprise funding biotech **start-ups and innovation**.
- **BRIC (Biotechnology Research and Innovation Council, 2024)** — a single apex autonomous society formed by **merging 14 DBT autonomous institutes** to reduce fragmentation.

## BioE3 Policy (2024)

- Full form: **Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment**; approved by the **Union Cabinet in August 2024**.
- Promotes **high-performance biomanufacturing**, biofoundries and bio-AI hubs.
- Thematic focus areas include bio-based chemicals & enzymes, functional foods, precision biotherapeutics, climate-resilient agriculture, carbon capture and marine/space biotech.
- Vision: support India's transition to a **bio-based, circular economy** and a net-zero pathway.
keyPoints: DBT is India's nodal biotech department; BIRAC funds biotech start-ups and innovation.
BRIC (2024) merged 14 DBT autonomous institutes into one apex society.
BioE3 Policy (2024) = Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment, approved by the Union Cabinet.
BioE3 promotes high-performance biomanufacturing, biofoundries and bio-based products.
BioE3 supports India's move toward a bio-based, circular economy and net-zero goals.
items.source: PIB / DBT — BioE3 Policy (2024) and BRIC establishment

items.title: Medical biotech, vaccines & Genome India
items.body:
## Vaccines & therapies

- **Covaxin (BBV152)** — India's indigenous **inactivated-virus** COVID-19 vaccine (Bharat Biotech + ICMR-NIV).
- **ZyCoV-D** (Zydus Cadila) — the **world's first approved DNA vaccine** for humans; needle-free, intradermal.
- **Gene therapy** corrects disease-causing genes; **stem cells**, **biosimilars** and **personalised (precision) medicine** are growing areas.

## Genome India Project (GIP)

- Launched **January 2020**, funded by **DBT**, coordinated with **IISc Centre for Brain Research** and 20+ institutions.
- Goal: sequence **10,000 Indian genomes** (phase 1) to build an **Indian reference genome** capturing the country's genetic diversity.
- Completion of 10,000-genome sequencing was announced in **2025**, enabling precision-medicine and disease-prediction research.
keyPoints: Covaxin is India's indigenous inactivated-virus COVID-19 vaccine (Bharat Biotech + ICMR).
ZyCoV-D by Zydus Cadila is the world's first approved DNA vaccine for humans (needle-free).
Genome India Project (launched 2020, DBT-funded) targets 10,000 Indian genomes in phase 1.
GIP is coordinated with the IISc Centre for Brain Research and 20+ institutions.
Completion of 10,000-genome sequencing under GIP was announced in 2025 for precision medicine.
items.source: PIB / ICMR — COVID-19 vaccines; DBT — Genome India Project

items.title: Nanotechnology — scale, materials & applications
items.body:
## The nanoscale

- **1 nanometre (nm) = 10⁻⁹ m** (one-billionth of a metre). At this scale, materials show **new optical, electrical and mechanical properties**.
- India's **Nano Mission (2007)**, under the **DST**, funds nanoscience research, infrastructure and human resources.

## Key nanomaterials

| Material | Feature |
|---|---|
| **Graphene** | Single-atom-thick carbon sheet; superb conductor |
| **Carbon nanotubes** | Very high tensile strength; conductive |
| **Quantum dots** | Semiconductor nanocrystals; colour depends on size |

## Applications & concerns

- **Medicine**: targeted drug delivery, diagnostics, imaging.
- **Electronics**: smaller, faster chips; displays.
- **Environment/other**: water-purification membranes, stronger textiles, better catalysts and energy storage.
- **Nanotoxicity** — the possible health and environmental risks of engineered nanoparticles — is an active safety concern.
keyPoints: 1 nanometre = one-billionth of a metre; matter shows new properties at the nanoscale.
India's Nano Mission (2007) is run by the Department of Science and Technology (DST).
Graphene is a single layer of carbon; carbon nanotubes have very high tensile strength.
Quantum dots are semiconductor nanocrystals whose emitted colour depends on their size.
Nanotech aids drug delivery, electronics, water purification and textiles; nanotoxicity is a safety concern.

items.title: Bioethics, IPR & Andhra Pradesh ecosystem
items.body:
## Ethics, biosafety & IPR

- **Cartagena Protocol** (under CBD) — safe **transboundary movement of living modified organisms (LMOs)**.
- **Nagoya Protocol** (under CBD) — **access to genetic resources** and fair, equitable **benefit-sharing**.
- **Biopiracy** — unauthorised commercial use of biological resources/traditional knowledge; countered by India's **Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (amended 2023)** and the traditional-knowledge digital library.
- Concerns: GM safety, patents on life forms, gene-editing of human embryos (**germline editing** ethics).

## Andhra Pradesh & regional biotech

- **AMTZ (Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone), Visakhapatnam** — India's first dedicated **medical-devices manufacturing** park, cutting import dependence.
- **Genome Valley** (Hyderabad region) — a large biotech/life-sciences cluster adjoining the state.
keyPoints: Cartagena Protocol governs safe transboundary movement of living modified organisms.
Nagoya Protocol covers access to genetic resources and fair benefit-sharing (both under the CBD).
India's Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (amended 2023) checks biopiracy and implements CBD obligations.
AMTZ Visakhapatnam is India's first dedicated medical-devices manufacturing park.
Genome Valley near Hyderabad is a major regional biotech/life-sciences cluster.
items.source: CBD Secretariat; MoEFCC — Biological Diversity Act; Govt of AP — AMTZ

items.title: Applied Genetics — Barcoding, Inheritance, Bt Cotton & Vaccine Platforms
items.body:
## DNA barcoding vs DNA fingerprinting

- **DNA barcoding** identifies species using a short, standard gene region (e.g. **CO1**). It can **distinguish look-alike species** and **detect undesirable plant/animal material in processed foods** — but it **cannot assess the age** of an organism.
- **DNA fingerprinting** (CCMB Hyderabad; Lalji Singh) identifies individuals for forensics/paternity.

## Mitochondrial inheritance

- **Mitochondrial DNA is inherited entirely from the mother**; a child can inherit mitochondrial disease from the mother.
- **Mitochondrial Replacement Therapy** (before/after IVF) can prevent passing on such disease — the basis of the **'three-parent baby'**.

## GM crops & Bt cotton

- **Bollgard I and Bollgard II** are **Bt cotton** technologies (Monsanto) using **Cry** genes (Cry1Ac; Cry2Ab) from *Bacillus thuringiensis* for bollworm resistance — **India's only commercially cultivated GM crop**.
- Regulator: **GEAC** (under MoEFCC); **Cartagena Protocol** governs Living Modified Organisms (LMOs).

## Cloning & vaccine platforms

- **SCNT (Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer)** is used for **reproductive cloning** of animals (Dolly the sheep, 1996).
- **Recombinant vector vaccines** use genetic engineering, employing **bacteria and viruses as vectors**.

## Nanoparticles

- **Natural nanoparticles exist** (soot, volcanic ash); metallic-oxide nanoparticles are used in **cosmetics/sunscreen**; some commercial nanoparticles entering the environment can be **unsafe** (nanotoxicity, free radicals).
keyPoints: DNA barcoding identifies species and detects adulterants in food but cannot assess an organism's age.
Mitochondrial DNA is maternally inherited; mitochondrial replacement therapy (three-parent baby) prevents transmission.
Bollgard I/II are Bt cotton technologies using Cry genes; Bt cotton is India's only commercial GM crop.
GEAC (MoEFCC) regulates GMOs; Cartagena Protocol covers Living Modified Organisms.
SCNT is used for reproductive cloning (Dolly, 1996); recombinant vector vaccines use bacteria/viruses as vectors.
Natural nanoparticles (soot, ash) exist; metallic-oxide nanoparticles are used in cosmetics; some pose nanotoxicity risks.
